summary: Dependency-confusion beacon posts host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a postinstall script (beacon.cjs) and a main entry (index.js) that both POST installer-side identifiers — hostname, install path, cwd, and Node version — to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires automatically on `npm install` via `scripts.postinstall` and again on `require()` of the module. The shipped index.js is a Proxy returning no-op functions for any property access, giving the package no legitimate runtime function beyond reporting that the install occurred. The README self-labels the package as an 'authorized dependency-confusion test', but the behavior is unconsented collection of host identifiers from the installing machine and transmission to a non-publisher bare-IP endpoint with no TLS and no publisher relationship. The scoped namespace plus the implausibly high version number (99.0.1) are consistent with a dependency-confusion resolution-winning shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
